Plotting EEG and stimuli¶

This step is optional, but it's a good idea to visualize the EEG data and predictors and check the time alignment between the predictors before moving on to specifying your TRF model.

Visualizing EEG, waveform, and predictors¶

The ns.trf.plot_schematic() function allows you to do this easily:

In [2]:
Copied! 
import neuraspeech as ns
import neuraspeech as ns
In [3]:
Copied! 
# Path to the EEG data file you want to plot
eeg_path = 'examples/sub-3000_04_ses-1_task-alice.pickle'

# Path to the stimulus directory
stim_path = '../../neuraspeech/trf/stim/alice'

# Path to the predictor set directory
predictor_set_path = '../../neuraspeech/trf/predictors/acou_pred_set'

# Which stimulus to plot?
stim_to_plot = 'track1.wav'

ns.trf.plot_schematic(
    to_plot = ['eeg', 'waveform', 'gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8'], 
    eeg_path = eeg_path, 
    stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, 
    time_window = (0, 3), # Show the first 3 seconds of the everything
    stim_path = stim_path,
    predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path
    )
# Path to the EEG data file you want to plot eeg_path = 'examples/sub-3000_04_ses-1_task-alice.pickle' # Path to the stimulus directory stim_path = '../../neuraspeech/trf/stim/alice' # Path to the predictor set directory predictor_set_path = '../../neuraspeech/trf/predictors/acou_pred_set' # Which stimulus to plot? stim_to_plot = 'track1.wav' ns.trf.plot_schematic( to_plot = ['eeg', 'waveform', 'gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8'], eeg_path = eeg_path, stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, time_window = (0, 3), # Show the first 3 seconds of the everything stim_path = stim_path, predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path )

In addition to the paths, the main argument is to_plot. By setting it to ['eeg', 'waveform', 'gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8'], we'll plot the EEG waveform (each line representing a channel), audio waveform, and the 8-band gammatone envelope and onsets in the order listed. Predictor names should match the part of the predictor filename after the ~ and before the file extension (e.g., 'track1~gammatone-8.pickle'). Any item in to_plot other than 'eeg' or 'waveform' is interpreted as a predictor name and the function will try to load it loaded from predictor_set_path.

Check if the stimulus waveform and predictors are properly aligned. For example, you should see a narrow vertical stripe in the 8-band gammatone onset predictor when the audio waveform transitions from silence to voiced activity. If the alignment looks incorrect, first check whether there are any issues in the predictor generation step.

Pro tips¶

1. Customizing your plots¶

The function is named plot_schematic() because it can generate a schematic figure illustrating the EEG and time-aligned stimulus features, which canb be useful for poster presentations, slides, and publications. For these purposes, it is often helpful to create a more polished figure and have better control over the plot aesthetics. ns.trf.plot_schematic() includes several optional arguments for customizing the figure. The key idea is that most of these arguments should be provided as lists whose values match the order of the items in to_plot (use None a placeholder when you want to keep the default setting for a particular item).

Below are a few usage examples. Feel free to play around with them.

In [4]:
Copied! 
ns.trf.plot_schematic(
    to_plot = ['eeg', 'waveform', 'gammatone-1', 'gammatone-on-1', 'gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8', 'lexical-surprisal'], 
    eeg_path = eeg_path, 
    stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, 
    time_window = (0, 3),
    stim_path = stim_path,
    predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path,

    ## Other optional plotting parameters ##

    # Output figure path
    # If show_colorbar is True, will also save the colorbars as separate figures in the same folder
    output_fig_path = 'examples/example_schematic.svg',

    # The saved figure will have a transparent background if True.
    transparent_background = True,

    # Figure size
    figsize = (12, 12),

    # Colorbars for 2D predictor plots
    show_colorbar = True,

    # Relative heights of the subplots (must match the number of subplots)
    height_ratios = [0.8, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.8],

    # Colors for each subplot. Can be color names, hex codes, or colormap names. 
    # Whether they are color names or colormap names will be automatically inferred based on plot type.
    # See here for colormap reference: https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/colors/colormaps.html
    colors =  ['Spectral', 'gray', '#fc4400', '#fc4400', 'inferno', 'inferno', '#385D94'],

    # Line widths for each subplot
    linewidths =  [2.0, 0.3, 1.75, 1.75, None, None, 3.0],

    # Y-axis labels (use None for no labels)
    ylabels = ['Amplitude', 'Amplitude', None, None, 'Frequency [Hz]', 'Frequency [Hz]', 'Surprisal [bits]'],

    # Titles for subplots
    titles = ['EEG', 'Waveform', 'Broadband envelope', 'Broadband onsets', 'Multiband envelope', 'Multiband onsets', 'Lexical surprisal'],

    # Whtether to hide y-axis ticks for each subplot
    hide_y_ticks = [False, False, False, False, True, True, False],

    # Plot the lexical surprisal as impulses (vertical lines) instead of a continuous line. 
    as_impulses = [False, False, False, False, False, False, True],
    )
ns.trf.plot_schematic( to_plot = ['eeg', 'waveform', 'gammatone-1', 'gammatone-on-1', 'gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8', 'lexical-surprisal'], eeg_path = eeg_path, stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, time_window = (0, 3), stim_path = stim_path, predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path, ## Other optional plotting parameters ## # Output figure path # If show_colorbar is True, will also save the colorbars as separate figures in the same folder output_fig_path = 'examples/example_schematic.svg', # The saved figure will have a transparent background if True. transparent_background = True, # Figure size figsize = (12, 12), # Colorbars for 2D predictor plots show_colorbar = True, # Relative heights of the subplots (must match the number of subplots) height_ratios = [0.8, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.8], # Colors for each subplot. The example below further shows that you can:

  1. Annotate the plot with the TextGrid of the stimulus
  2. Use custom colormap
  3. Have additional control options for y-axis
  4. Add vertical mark lines
In [5]:
Copied! 
# TextGrid configuration
# Required keys are 'textgrid_path', 'tier_name', and 'axes_to_annotate'
annotate_textgrid = {
    # Path to the directory containing TextGrid files
    'textgrid_path': '../../neuraspeech/trf/stim/alice_textgrids',

    # Name of the tier to annotate (must match the tier name in the TextGrid)
    'tier_name': 'phones',

    # A indices of the axes to annotate
    'axes_to_annotate': [2, 3],

    # Vertical position of the labels (0 = bottom, 1 = top)
    'y_loc': 0.95,

    # Font size for the labels
    'labelsize': 10,

    # Transparency
    'alpha': 0.9,

    # Labels to exclude from the annotation (e.g., silence labels)
    'remove_labels': ["sil"],

    # Apply a regex pattern to remove labels (e.g., to sress marks 0, 1, or 2 at the end)
    'remove_regex': "[012]$",
    
    'labelsize': 11,
    'color': '#BA274A'
}

# Custom colormap
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
custom_colormap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    'custom_colormap',
    ['#453E79','#5C53A2', '#8E86C1','#F1B26A', '#EC9532', '#BB6C11']
)

# Configurations for adding vertical mark lines
# Required keys are 'times' and 'axes_to_annotate'
vlines = {
    # Times (in seconds) where vertical lines should be drawn
    'times': [0.5, 2.0],

    # Indices of the axes to annotate with vertical lines
    'axes_to_annotate': [2, 3],
    
    'color': 'black',
    'linestyle': '--'
}
# TextGrid configuration # Required keys are 'textgrid_path', 'tier_name', and 'axes_to_annotate' annotate_textgrid = { # Path to the directory containing TextGrid files 'textgrid_path': '../../neuraspeech/trf/stim/alice_textgrids', # Name of the tier to annotate (must match the tier name in the TextGrid) 'tier_name': 'phones', # A indices of the axes to annotate 'axes_to_annotate': [2, 3], # Vertical position of the labels (0 = bottom, 1 = top) 'y_loc': 0.95, # Font size for the labels 'labelsize': 10, # Transparency 'alpha': 0.9, # Labels to exclude from the annotation (e.g., silence labels) 'remove_labels': ["sil"], # Apply a regex pattern to remove labels (e.g., to sress marks 0, 1, or 2 at the end) 'remove_regex': "[012]$", 'labelsize': 11, 'color': '#BA274A' } # Custom colormap from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap custom_colormap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list( 'custom_colormap', ['#453E79','#5C53A2', '#8E86C1','#F1B26A', '#EC9532', '#BB6C11'] ) # Configurations for adding vertical mark lines # Required keys are 'times' and 'axes_to_annotate' vlines = { # Times (in seconds) where vertical lines should be drawn 'times': [0.5, 2.0], # Indices of the axes to annotate with vertical lines 'axes_to_annotate': [2, 3], 'color': 'black', 'linestyle': '--' }
In [6]:
Copied! 
ns.trf.plot_schematic(
    to_plot = ['gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8', 'pitch-mel', 'waveform', 'eeg'], 
    eeg_path = eeg_path, 
    stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, 
    time_window = (0, 3),
    stim_path = stim_path,
    predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path,

    ## Other optional plotting parameters ##

    output_fig_path = 'examples/example_schematic_2.svg',
    figsize = (12, 10),
    show_colorbar = True,
    height_ratios = [0.5, 0.5, 0.6, 1, 0.7],

    # Colors for each subplot. Can be color names, hex codes, or colormap names. 
    # Apply the custom colormap to the 2nd and 5th plots
    colors =  ['Spectral', custom_colormap, '#ED9B40', 'lightgray', custom_colormap],

    linewidths =  [None, None, 3.5, 1.0, 2.0],
    ylabels = ['Frequency [Hz]', 'Frequency [Hz]', 'Pitch [Mel]', 'Amplitude', 'Amplitude'],

    # Treat zeros as NaNs for the 3rd plot (pitch-mel)
    zeros_as_nans = [False, False, True, False, False], 

    # Annotate the 3rd plot (pitch-mel) with a TextGrid
    annotate_textgrid = annotate_textgrid,

    # Some control options for the y-axis ticks and labels:
    # Colors for the y-axis labels (use None for default color)
    y_axis_colors = [None, None, '#ED9B40', None, '#5C53A2'],

    # Turn off y-axis ticks for 1st and 2nd plots
    hide_y_ticks = [True, True, False, False, False],

    # Place the y-axis on the right side for the 3rd plot
    y_axis_on_right = [False, False, True, False, False],

    # Adjust the y-axis spine offsets for better visibility
    y_axis_offsets = [None, None, 8, None, None],

    # Hide the y-axis for the 4th plot (waveform)
    hide_y_axis = [False, False, False, True, False],

    # Adding vertical lines
    vlines = vlines
    )
ns.trf.plot_schematic( to_plot = ['gammatone-8', 'gammatone-on-8', 'pitch-mel', 'waveform', 'eeg'], eeg_path = eeg_path, stim_to_plot = stim_to_plot, time_window = (0, 3), stim_path = stim_path, predictor_set_path = predictor_set_path, ## Other optional plotting parameters ## output_fig_path = 'examples/example_schematic_2.svg', figsize = (12, 10), show_colorbar = True, height_ratios = [0.5, 0.5, 0.6, 1, 0.7], # Colors for each subplot.
